mainTopic: Who is believed about facts only they know (a seller, a judge, a בכור, a שתוקי's mother), and a new משנה on whether people of flawed lineage may marry each other.
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא about people believed on facts only they know. A seller is believed about whom he sold to when both people paid him. A judge is believed about his ruling while the litigants are still before him, in a שודא דדייני case where the written verdicts were torn. רב נחמן then lists three people believed about a בכור: a midwife, the mother and the father, each for a different length of time. רבי יהודה extends the father's word even to calling a son a בן גרושה, and חכמים disagree. Next the גמרא explains אבא שאול's term 'בדוקי'. The mother is believed that the father was fit even where most men around her are unfit, and רבא rules like אבא שאול. A new משנה asks whether people barred from the קהל may marry each other, with views from רבי יהודה and רבי אליעזר. The גמרא raises problems with how to read that משנה, and רב יהודה's answer begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not just check whose money the seller took?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the seller's word is needed. We could simply see whose money he took.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see from whom he took the money!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא said the seller is believed to say 'I sold to this one and not to that one.' The גמרא now asks why we need his word at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whoever paid is obviously the buyer. So the seller's credibility seems unnecessary. The גמרא is pushing for a case where his word really matters.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us see (check)
Money, coins
He took, he holds

phrases.english: But let us see from whom he took the money!
phrases.notes: 'He' is the seller from the ברייתא: whoever paid him should be the buyer.

steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the seller is believed about whom he sold to.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The facts can be checked by seeing whose money he holds, so his testimony seems unnecessary.

steps.title: He took money from both buyers
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed when the seller took money from both people. One he took willingly and one against his will, and we don't know which was which.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where he took money from both of them and said: 'One I took willingly and one against my will.' It is not known which was willing and which was not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the money alone can't tell us who bought the item. Both people paid him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both men handed over money, so checking the money proves nothing. Only the seller knows which payment he agreed to. That is why we need his word.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (the case of)
From both of them
With my consent, willingly
Against my will

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he took money from both of them and said:
one I took willingly, and one against my will.
And it is not known which was with his consent
and which was without his consent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Checking the money would show who the buyer is.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both people paid, so only the seller's word can decide.

steps.title: A judge is believed about his ruling
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. A judge is believed to say whom he ruled for and against, but only while the litigants are still before him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A judge is believed to say: 'I ruled this one innocent and this one liable.' When is this said? When the litigants are standing before him. But if they are not standing before him, he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next case in the ברייתא, which follows the same idea as the seller. This time it is a judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judge is like the seller holding the item. He is believed while the matter is still 'in his hands,' with the litigants in front of him. Once they leave, his word alone is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Judge
I ruled in favor of
I ruled against, found liable
Litigants
In what case is this said?

phrases.english: A judge is believed to say:
this one I found innocent, and this one I found liable.
In what case is this said?
When the litigants are standing before him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין בַּעֲלֵי דִינִים עוֹמְדִים לְפָנָיו –
phrases.english: But if the litigants are not standing before him,
he is not believed.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge is believed about his verdict only while the litigants stand before him.

steps.title: Why not just check who holds the written verdict?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need the judge's word. We could look at who holds the written ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see who holds the written verdict!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the same kind of challenge it made about the seller. Why rely on the judge when there is a written verdict?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The winner of a case usually gets a document showing he won. If we can see who holds it, the judge's statement seems unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: A written verdict showing who won

phrases.english: But let us see who holds the written verdict!

steps.kashyaTarget: The need to believe the judge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A written verdict would prove who won, so the judge's testimony seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The written verdicts were torn
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed when the written verdicts were torn up and can't be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where their written verdicts were torn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by setting up a case where no document is left to check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the papers destroyed, nothing shows who won. Only the judge can tell us.

keyTerms.meaning: That was torn

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where their written verdicts were torn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The written verdict can show who won.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verdicts were torn, so there is nothing to check.

steps.title: Why not just judge the case again?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the judge can't simply hear the case again and rule the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him judge them again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. Even without the papers, the judge could just rehear the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the law led to one result the first time, a new trial should give the same result. Then we wouldn't need to rely on the judge's memory at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him go back (do it again)
And let him judge them

phrases.english: But let him go back and judge them again!

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the verdicts were torn.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A new trial should repeat the same verdict, so no testimony is needed.

steps.title: The case was decided by judges' discretion
steps.stepSummary: The case was one of שודא דדייני, where the result depends on the judge's personal sense. A rehearing might come out differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a case of the judges' discretion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this was a case with no clear legal answer. The judge decided by his own judgment, so a new trial won't necessarily match the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a שודא דדייני case, the judge simply decides who seems more deserving. Judging again could produce a different result. So only his testimony tells us what he actually ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: The judges' discretion: a ruling based on the judge's own sense, not a clear rule

steps.whatToRemember: For both the seller and the judge, the גמרא keeps narrowing the case until only that person's word can settle the matter.

phrases.english: It was a case of the judges' discretion.
phrases.notes: Literally 'the judges' throw': the judge decides by his own sense, so a second ruling might not match.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why a new trial won't help.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rehearing the case would repeat the same verdict.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a discretion case, a new ruling may differ, so we need the judge's word.

steps.title: Three people are believed about a בכור
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says a midwife, a father, and a mother are believed about which child is the בכור, each for a different length of time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Three are believed about a firstborn: the midwife, his father, and his mother. The midwife only right away, his mother all seven days, and his father forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב נחמן about who can tell us which child is the בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person is believed for a different length of time. The midwife is believed only right at the birth. The mother is believed for the first seven days. The father is believed forever.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn son
Midwife
Immediately
Forever

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Three are believed about a firstborn,
and they are: a midwife, his father, and his mother.
A midwife: only immediately;
his mother: all seven days;
his father: forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: שְׁלֹשָׁה נֶאֱמָנִין עַל הַבְּכוֹר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A midwife is believed immediately, a mother for seven days, and a father forever, about which child is the בכור.

steps.title: The father's source: 'he shall acknowledge'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק 'יכיר' to mean the father identifies the בכור to others. This supports the father being believed forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'He shall acknowledge' means he shall make him known to others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רב נחמן's rule about the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה itself gives the father the power to identify his בכור to others. That is why his word counts forever, and not just for a limited time like the others.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
He shall acknowledge, recognize

steps.whatToRemember: The father is believed about his בכור forever, based on the פסוק 'יכיר'.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
'He shall acknowledge': he shall make him known to others.

steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's rule that the father is believed forever.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading of the פסוק 'יכיר' (דברים 21:17).

steps.title: רבי יהודה extends the father's credibility; חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק 'יכיר', רבי יהודה rules that a father is believed to say which son is his בכור. He is also believed to say a son is a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה. חכמים say he is not believed about those.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here רבי יהודה said: a person is believed to say 'This is my firstborn son.' Just as he is believed to say that, he is also believed to say 'This is the son of a divorcee' or 'This is the son of a חלוצה.' The Rabbis say: he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 9 finishes. רבי יהודה stretches the father's believability to cases that make a son unfit for כהונה, and חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone accepts that the פסוק 'יכיר' makes the father believed about which son is the בכור. The argument is only about whether this believability goes further, so that the father could also hurt his son's lineage. רבי יהודה says yes; חכמים limit it to naming the בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Believed; his word is accepted
Son of a divorcee (born to a כהן), unfit for כהונה
Son of a woman who had חליצה (born to a כהן), unfit for כהונה
The Rabbis, the majority opinion

phrases.english: From here Rabbi Yehuda said:
A person is believed to say: "This is my firstborn son."
And just as he is believed to say: "This is my firstborn son,"
so too he is believed to say: "This is the son of a divorcee"
and "This is the son of a chalutza."
And the Rabbis say: he is not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from step 9 by drawing a ruling from the פסוק and recording a disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a father is believed about the בכור and also to call a son a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה. חכמים: he is not believed about the latter.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees the father is believed to name the בכור. רבי יהודה and חכמים argue only about whether he can also make his son unfit for כהונה.

steps.title: What does אבא שאול mean by 'בדוקי'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes אבא שאול from the משנה, who called a שתוקי a 'בדוקי', and asks what that word means.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול used to call a שתוקי 'בדוקי.' What does 'בדוקי' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line from the משנה and asks what אבא שאול's word 'בדוקי' means. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שתוקי is a child whose father is unknown. 'בדוקי' means 'checked', so the question is who gets checked, and what that check accomplishes.

keyTerms.meaning: A child who knows his mother but not his father (literally 'silenced one')
'Checked one', אבא שאול's name for a שתוקי
A תנא quoted in the משנה

phrases.english: Abba Shaul used to call
a shetuki "beduki."
What does "beduki" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of אבא שאול's term 'בדוקי'.

steps.title: If it means checking the mother, that was already taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'בדוקי' means we question the mother, and she is believed if she says the father was of proper lineage. But that matches רבן גמליאל, and his view was already taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means we check with his mother, and if she says 'I was with a man of proper lineage' she is believed: whose view is that? רבן גמליאל's. But we already learned that once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible meaning of 'בדוקי' and right away challenges it: this would just repeat something already taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בדוקי means the mother is believed about the father, then אבא שאול is simply following רבן גמליאל. A משנה should not teach the same law twice, so this meaning seems to leave אבא שאול with nothing new to say.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say', which introduces a suggestion the גמרא is about to challenge
'I was with a man of proper lineage'
'We already learned this once', a challenge that something is repeated

phrases.english: If you say it means that they check with his mother
and if she says: "I was with a man of proper lineage," she is believed,
whose view is that? Rabban Gamliel's,
but we already learned this once!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to step 11 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of בדוקי as 'the mother is checked and believed'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading makes אבא שאול repeat רבן גמליאל's ruling, which is already taught elsewhere.

steps.title: The משנה in כתובות where the mother is believed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the משנה in כתובות as the place this was already taught. A pregnant woman says the father is a כהן. רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר believe her, רבי יהושע does not, and שמואל rules like רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: a woman was pregnant, and they asked her what the status of the fetus was. She said: from so-and-so, and he is a כהן. רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed. רבי יהושע says we do not rely on her word. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the mother's believability was already taught, which backs up the challenge in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה already says that a woman's claim about the father's good lineage is accepted, and the הלכה follows that view. So if בדוקי meant the same thing, אבא שאול would be adding nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Pregnant
What is its nature or status?
'We do not live by her mouth', meaning we don't rely on her word
The final ruling follows this opinion

phrases.english: As we learned: if she was pregnant,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ לָהּ: מָה טִיבוֹ שֶׁל עוּבָּר זֶה?
phrases.english: and they said to her: What is the status of this fetus?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לָהֶם: מֵאִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי וְכֹהֵן הוּא.
phrases.english: She said to them: From so-and-so, and he is a kohen.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמֶנֶת,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say: She is believed,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִפִּיהָ אָנוּ חַיִּין.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehoshua says: We do not live by her mouth.
And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabban Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that the challenge in step 12 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: That the mother's believability was already taught.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in כתובות 13a and שמואל's ruling like רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: One ruling for the mother, one for her daughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is no repeat. The משנה in כתובות makes the mother herself fit, and אבא שאול teaches that her daughter is fit too.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ruling is to make her fit, and one is to make her daughter fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving each ruling its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל's ruling in כתובות is about the woman herself being allowed to marry a כהן. אבא שאול's 'בדוקי' adds that her claim also makes her child fit.

keyTerms.meaning: To make fit, here meaning allowed to marry a כהן
Her daughter

phrases.english: One is to make her fit,
and one is to make her daughter fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא לְהַכְשִׁיר בָּהּ, וַחֲדָא לְהַכְשִׁיר בְּבִתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'already taught' challenge of steps 12 and 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source covers a different person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources teach the same law about the mother.
steps.terutzMaskana: כתובות covers the mother, and אבא שאול covers the daughter.

steps.title: But one opinion already makes the daughter fit too
steps.stepSummary: The answer works if רבן גמליאל only made the mother fit. But according to the view that he makes the daughter fit too, what does אבא שאול add?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says that רבן גמליאל, who makes her fit, still disqualifies her daughter. But according to the one who says that he makes her daughter fit as well, what is אבא שאול coming to teach us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. That answer only works according to one opinion about how far רבן גמליאל's ruling reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a disagreement about whether רבן גמליאל's ruling also covers the daughter. If it does not, אבא שאול adds the daughter. If it does, the daughter is already covered, and the problem of repetition comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This works well', which sets up a 'but according to the other view' challenge
Disqualifies, makes unfit
What is he coming to teach us?

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says:
According to the one who makes her fit, he disqualifies her daughter.
phrases.notes: 'The one who makes her fit' is רבן גמליאל from the משנה in כתובות.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says:
According to the one who makes her fit, he makes her daughter fit too,
what is Abba Shaul coming to teach us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 14 works only according to one opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that אבא שאול adds the daughter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבן גמליאל already makes the daughter fit, אבא שאול's ruling is again a repeat.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is rejecting רבן גמליאל here. It is only asking how far his ruling reaches, and whether that leaves anything new for אבא שאול to teach.

steps.title: Why אבא שאול still adds something
steps.stepSummary: Even if רבן גמליאל makes the daughter fit, אבא שאול goes further. He believes the mother even where most men around her would make the child unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול's teaching goes further than רבן גמליאל's. If we only had רבן גמליאל, I would have said she is believed only where most men around her are fit. Where most men around her are unfit, I might say she is not believed. So אבא שאול's teaching was needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15. אבא שאול adds a harder case that רבן גמליאל's case does not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבן גמליאל's case, most men the woman could have been with are fit, so believing her goes along with the majority. אבא שאול believes her even when most men around her are unfit, so her word goes against the majority. That is a new חידוש, so his teaching is not a repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes further; is stronger
I would have said (an early assumption that turns out wrong)
Most are fit
Most are unfit
It was needed; the teaching is not extra

steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל believes the mother where the majority supports her claim. אבא שאול believes her even against the majority.

phrases.english: For Abba Shaul's teaching goes further than Rabban Gamliel's.
For if we had it only from there, I would have said:
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה in כתובות about the pregnant woman, from step 13.

phrases.english: There, where most men are fit with regard to her, she is believed,
but where most men are unfit with regard to her,
I might say she is not believed. So it was needed.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a case that only the second source covers (צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without אבא שאול, we would believe the mother only where most men around her are fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: אבא שאול teaches that she is believed even where most men around her are unfit.

steps.title: רבא rules like אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the הלכה follows אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה follows אבא שאול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final הלכה for this topic. We follow אבא שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that אבא שאול's view is the broadest, since the mother is believed even against the majority. רבא rules that this broad view is the הלכה, so the mother is believed even in that harder case.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא said (an אמורא)
The practical law
Following אבא שאול

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows אבא שאול. The mother is believed that her child is fit, even where most men around her are unfit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the long discussion of שתוקי and בדוקי with a practical ruling.

phrases.english: Rava said: The halacha follows Abba Shaul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling after the explanation of אבא שאול's view

steps.title: New משנה: may people of flawed lineage marry each other
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that everyone forbidden to marry into the קהל may marry one another. רבי יהודה forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: All those who are forbidden to enter the קהל may marry one another. רבי יהודה forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. The first opinion allows people who cannot marry into regular Jewish families to marry each other, and רבי יהודה disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Entering the קהל' means marrying a regular Jew of proper lineage. The תנא קמא says that being barred from that does not stop such people from marrying each other. רבי יהודה forbids it, and the גמרא will explain his reason later.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, our משנה
Those forbidden to enter the congregation, meaning to marry a Jew of proper lineage
One with another; with each other
Forbids

phrases.english: MISHNAH: All those who are forbidden to enter the congregation,
phrases.notes: 'Enter the congregation' means marry a regular Jew of proper lineage.

phrases.english: are permitted to marry one another.
Rabbi Yehuda forbids it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those forbidden to enter the קהל may marry each other. רבי יהודה forbids it.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: definite cases versus doubtful cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר allows two people whose flaw is definite to marry each other. He forbids any match where one or both have only a doubtful status. The doubtful ones are a שתוקי, an אסופי and a כותי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Definite cases with definite cases are permitted. Definite with doubtful, doubtful with definite, and doubtful with doubtful are forbidden. These are the doubtful ones: a שתוקי, an אסופי and a כותי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a third opinion, from רבי אליעזר. He splits people into definite cases and doubtful cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A definite case, such as a known ממזר, has a clear status, so two such people may marry. A doubtful person might actually be fully fit, so marrying them to a ממזר could be forbidden. Two doubtful people are also forbidden, since one might be fit and the other a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Definite cases, whose flawed status is known for sure
Doubtful cases, whose status is uncertain
Doubts; the doubtful ones
A foundling, a child found abandoned with no known parents
A Samaritan, whose Jewish status was in doubt

steps.confusionAlert: 'Doubtful' here describes the person's own lineage, which is unclear. It does not mean the משנה is unsure about the law.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Definite cases with definite cases are permitted,
definite with doubtful, and doubtful with definite,
and doubtful with doubtful are forbidden.
And these are the doubtful ones:
a shetuki, an asufi, and a Kuti.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: וַדָּאָן בְּוַדָּאָן – מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Definite cases may marry each other. Any match involving a doubtful case (שתוקי, אסופי, כותי) is forbidden.

steps.title: Who are 'all those forbidden to enter the congregation'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking who the משנה means by 'all those forbidden to enter the קהל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'all those forbidden to enter the קהל' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking which people the משנה's opening words refer to. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא tests one possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'all those' are vague. The גמרא wants to know exactly which groups are included, because the answer decides whether this משנה teaches something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא, the discussion on the משנה
What? What does it mean?
All; every

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ מַאי כׇּל הָאֲסוּרִין לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל?
phrases.english: GEMARA: What is meant by 'all those forbidden to enter the congregation'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה from step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which groups 'all those forbidden to enter the קהל' refers to

steps.title: That was already taught in the first משנה of the chapter
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה means ממזרים, נתינים, שתוקים and אסופים, that is a repeat. The first משנה of the פרק already said these may marry each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means ממזרים, נתינים, שתוקים and אסופים, the תנא already taught that in the first part: ממזרים, נתינים, שתוקים and אסופים may marry each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer to its own question and immediately attacks it. That reading would make our משנה a repeat of an earlier one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first משנה of this פרק already listed these four groups and allowed them to marry each other. A משנה should not repeat itself, so 'all those forbidden' must mean someone else. This pushes the גמרא to look for a different group.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)
ממזרים, children of a forbidden union
נתינים, descendants of the גבעונים
But he already taught it!
The first part; the opening clause

phrases.english: If you say it means mamzerim, Gibeonites, shetukim, and foundlings,
but he already taught it in the first part,
phrases.notes: 'The first part' means the opening משנה of this פרק, which listed the groups that came up from בבל.

phrases.english: that mamzerim, Gibeonites, shetukim, and foundlings
are permitted to marry one another!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא מַמְזֵירֵי וּנְתִינֵי שְׁתוּקֵי וַאֲסוּפֵי הָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one answer to the שאלה of step 20 and rejects it
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'all those forbidden' means ממזרים, נתינים, שתוקים and אסופים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading would make our משנה repeat the first משנה of the פרק, which already allowed these groups to marry each other.

steps.title: A second problem: what does רבי יהודה forbid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds another difficulty and asks which case רבי יהודה's 'אוסר' refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: 'רבי יהודה forbids.' Which case is he forbidding?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second problem with how we read the משנה. It asks which marriage רבי יהודה forbids, and this sets up the possible answers in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first problem (step 21) was that the משנה would be repeating the first משנה of the פרק. Now the גמרא looks at רבי יהודה's dissent. If we cannot find a case for him to forbid, the reading of the משנה is in trouble again.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (introduces another difficulty)
On which one? Which case does this refer to?
Forbids

phrases.english: And furthermore: 'רבי יהודה forbids' — on which case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second difficulty alongside the repetition problem of step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific marriage is רבי יהודה forbidding in the משנה?

steps.title: It can't be definite with doubtful, because that is רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה forbids definite flaws marrying doubtful ones, that is exactly רבי אליעזר's later opinion. Since the משנה gives it to רבי אליעזר separately, רבי יהודה must not hold it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he forbids definite ones with doubtful ones, there is a problem. The latter clause teaches that רבי אליעזר says definite with definite is permitted, while definite with doubtful and doubtful with doubtful are forbidden. This shows that רבי יהודה does not hold this view!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one answer: maybe רבי יהודה forbids definite people marrying doubtful people. It rejects that answer right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That rule is said in the משנה by רבי אליעזר as his own separate opinion. If רבי יהודה already said the same thing, רבי אליעזר would add nothing new. So the way the משנה is set up shows that רבי יהודה does not hold this view.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (proposes an option, usually to reject it)
Those whose flawed status is definite (like a ממזר)
Those whose status is only doubtful (שתוקי, אסופי)
The latter clause of the משנה
By implication, it follows that

phrases.english: If you say: on definite ones marrying doubtful ones —
but since the latter clause teaches:
רבי אליעזר says:
definite ones with definite ones — permitted;
definite with doubtful, and doubtful with doubtful — forbidden;

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: this implies that רבי יהודה does not hold this!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא אַוַּדָּאָן בִּסְפֵיקָן – הָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries and rejects the first possible answer to the question of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי יהודה forbids definite flaws marrying doubtful ones.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That rule belongs to רבי אליעזר, who says it as a separate opinion. That implies רבי יהודה did not already say it.

steps.title: It can't be a גר with a ממזרת, because the משנה isn't discussing a גר
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רבי יהודה forbids a גר marrying a ממזרת. But the משנה only speaks about people forbidden to enter the קהל, and a גר is not one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say רבי יהודה forbids a גר with a ממזרת: does the משנה teach anything about a גר with a ממזרת? It teaches 'all those forbidden to enter the קהל'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second answer: maybe רבי יהודה forbids a convert marrying a ממזרת. It rejects this too, because the משנה never mentions a גר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's subject is 'all those forbidden to enter the קהל.' A גר is not in that group, so a ruling about a גר doesn't fit here. Now both readings of רבי יהודה have failed, which puts pressure on how we first read the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (brings up a possible answer)
A convert
A female ממזר
Does it teach anything about...? (meaning: it doesn't)

steps.whatToRemember: Neither option works for רבי יהודה: 'definite with doubtful' belongs to רבי אליעזר, and 'a גר with a ממזרת' is not the משנה's topic. Together with the repetition problem, this calls for a new reading of the משנה.

phrases.english: And if you would say:
רבי יהודה forbids a convert with a ממזרת —
Does it teach anything about a convert with a ממזרת?
It teaches 'all those forbidden to enter the congregation'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹסֵר אַגֵּר בְּמַמְזֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries and rejects the second possible answer after step 23 rejected the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי יהודה's prohibition refers to a גר marrying a ממזרת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה only talks about people forbidden to enter the קהל, and a גר is not in that group.

steps.title: רב יהודה begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה steps in to solve the difficulties about the משנה's wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only introduces a speaker. The גמרא is setting up רב יהודה's answer, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the repetition problem and the problem with רבי יהודה, the reading of the משנה needs fixing. רב יהודה is about to explain what the משנה really means so these problems go away.

keyTerms.meaning: רב יהודה said (an אמורא, a later sage)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רב יהודה (an אמורא who answers here) with רבי יהודה (the תנא in the משנה who is 'אוסר'). They are two different people.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the answer to the difficulties raised in steps 21 through 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading of the משנה's wording (its content continues past this line).
